source_version.submission_history_note: The arXiv abstract page observed during this audit lists only v1; no v2+ entry is present.

verified_claims.claim: HARD v1 contains an unresolved internal conflict between Table 1 HARD-Both static ASRs and the surrounding/introduction prose.
verified_claims.evidence: PDF printed page 7 Table 1 reports HARD-Both static ASR DPI/IPI/MC/SP = 12.1/1.3/13.9/7.4. The introduction on printed page 2 and the paragraph immediately below Table 1 instead state 15.4/1.0/6.7/10.2 for the same four named attack categories. Section 5.2 explicitly says each static-attack cell in Table 1 is a mean over four independent evaluation repeats, so the discrepancy cannot be dismissed as Table 1 being a single-run row without an additional undocumented aggregation distinction.

verified_claims.claim: The appendix prose also conflicts with Table 1 on memory-contamination and skill-poisoning UA.
verified_claims.evidence: PDF printed page 18 says HARD-Both attains MC/SP UA 86.3/92.0 while ASR is 6.7/10.2. Table 1 instead reports HARD-Both MC/SP UA 85.9/95.1 and ASR 13.9/7.4. No label in v1 identifies these prose numbers as a different split or aggregation.

verified_claims.claim: Table 3 provides partial internal evidence favoring the Table-1 memory-contamination row over the prose numbers, but does not resolve all static cells.
verified_claims.evidence: Table 3 is explicitly a HARD-Both memory-contamination evolution-backbone ablation under the same five-round budget. Its GLM-5.2 row is ASR/BU/UA = 13.9/94.7/85.9. The ASR 13.9 and UA 85.9 exactly match Table 1's HARD-Both MC values, whereas the prose/appendix use 6.7 and 86.3. This cross-table consistency makes Table 1 the better-supported v1 lineage for MC ASR/UA, but it is not an author correction and cannot resolve DPI/IPI/SP headline values. BU differs (94.7 in Table 3 versus 95.0 in Table 1), so the two tables are not byte-for-byte the same aggregate.

verified_claims.claim: On LPA, HARD-Policy outperforms HARD-Both on held-out ASR (4.8% vs 12.1%) and the paper attributes this reversal to routing pattern-matchable failures to the gate, reducing policy opportunities to learn transferable semantic principles.
verified_claims.evidence: Table 1 reports LPA ASR 4.8 for HARD-Policy and 12.1 for HARD-Both. Appendix case analysis on printed pages 17-18 repeats the held-out test-split values and explains that many pattern-matchable failures are routed to the gate evolver, leaving HARD-Both policy without the anti-obfuscation/cumulative-intent rules learned by HARD-Policy. The same appendix reports HARD-Both held-out/evolution split 12.1/7.3 and HARD-Policy 4.8/11.0.

verified_claims.claim: HARD-Gate improves strongly on its evolution split while only marginally on held-out LPA.
verified_claims.evidence: Appendix reports HARD-Gate evolution-split ASR 36.6% to 23.2% across five rounds, held-out test ASR 28.9% to 26.5%, and 30.9% without evolution. The paper interprets this as execution-level rules memorizing observed attacks with limited additional coverage of unseen adaptive behavior.

verified_claims.claim: The evolution-backbone ablation can reduce ASR while preserving attack-free BU yet collapse utility under attack.
verified_claims.evidence: Table 3, explicitly HARD-Both on memory contamination, reports No Evolution 63.9/88.1/57.8, GLM-5.2 13.9/94.7/85.9, Claude Opus-4.6 7.7/96.2/85.3, Qwen3.7-Max 13.5/96.4/74.1, and GPT-5.5 20.3/94.9/7.2 for ASR/BU/UA. The caption states all variants evolve five rounds with the same execution agent and judge model and different evolution backbones. Appendix implementation details additionally state execution agent, judges, benchmark tasks and evaluation protocol remain fixed and the evolution backbone is the only model varied.

scope_corrections: FE-041 is a reporting/provenance defect, not evidence that HARD fails. Static HARD-Both headline values from v1 should not be quoted as uniquely authoritative without identifying whether the number comes from Table 1 or prose.

For memory contamination specifically, Table 3 independently aligns with Table 1 on ASR=13.9 and UA=85.9 under the GLM-5.2 HARD-Both backbone, which is stronger internal support for those two Table-1 cells than for the conflicting prose values. This is only a partial lineage clue, not an author-issued correction.

FE-039 applies to the paper's LPA adaptive setting and its five-round held-out/evolution split. It does not show that joint policy+gate evolution is generally inferior; Table 1/static results order HARD-Both differently.

FE-040 applies to HARD-Both memory contamination under the paper's fixed five-round backbone-ablation harness. GPT-5.5's UA=7.2 is not a general claim about GPT-5.5 safety or utility outside this configuration.

The v1 paper reports static cells as four-repeat means and mentions per-cell standard deviation / pooled McNemar tests, but no author-linked raw repeat table or public HARD experiment artifact was located in this bounded audit.
